newsitem.title: GERMANY: Serb on trial in Germany on genocide charges.
newsitem.headline: Serb on trial in Germany on genocide charges.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb man went on trial in Germany on Friday on genocide charges, accused of leading death squads which massacred Moslems in 1992.
Nikola Jorgic, 50, is also charged with causing bodily harm and deprivation of liberty.

Jorgic, who had been living in the German city of Bochum, denies the charges. His lawyers say the case is one of mistaken identity. Their client could not have been involved in the crimes concerned as he was in prison at the time, they say.
Prosecutors allege Jorgic led a group of Serb nationalists from May to September 1992 and took part in at least 14 instances of "ethnic cleansing".
In one incident, Jorgic and an accomplice fired machineguns at a group of Moslems in the town of Grapska in June 1992, killing 22 people, prosecutors say.
German officials say they offered the case to the United Nations war crimes tribunal in the Hague but agreed to take it on themselves because the tribunal was overloaded with work.
The first Bosnian war crimes trial in Germany began on Tuesday.

A Bosnian Serb, Novislav Djajic, was charged with aiding murder and genocide. He stands accused of taking part in a June 1992 raid in which 14 Moslem men were killed and 15 others taken prisoner. The 15 were never seen again.
